session.goal: Implement the unfinished optional asset-weight task by packing the 52 nonbackground runtime companion, garden-prop, and lens-prop images into deterministic per-theme atlases while preserving garden behavior and measuring the reduced desktop image request count.

plan.summary: Replace the 52 independently loaded runtime sprites with deterministic light and dark atlases while retaining separate garden backgrounds, existing texture keys, rendering, and animation behavior.
plan.overview: Add a deterministic atlas build path using the existing checked-in runtime artwork, emit a small bounded set of per-theme atlas images plus frame metadata, and load each logical Phaser texture key from its corresponding atlas frame. Keep the two garden backgrounds as standalone images. Cover logical texture reachability and atlas construction with unit tests, then measure fresh desktop image requests and exercise garden behavior on desktop and mobile with light/dark visual inspection.
requirements: Pack all 52 nonbackground runtime companion, garden-prop, and lens-prop images from existing assets; do not regenerate artwork.
Use a small number of deterministic per-theme atlases and account for decoded texture size as well as HTTP request count.
Keep the light and dark garden backgrounds separate.
Preserve every existing logical texture key, light/dark texture selection, companion frame and sequence behavior, and garden/lens rendering.
Measure the fresh desktop garden image-request result after the change, starting from the recorded 54-image baseline.
Run typecheck, lint, unit tests, build, relevant desktop/mobile Playwright coverage, and inspect light/dark screenshots.
Do not push or merge product changes.
decisions: Use generated checked-in atlas artifacts and metadata derived only from current runtime WebP assets so Vite can import stable atlas URLs and Phaser can retain each existing logical texture key through atlas frame registration.
Bound atlas dimensions to avoid a request-count-only optimization that inflates decoded memory disproportionately; derive layout deterministically from ordered source definitions.
Keep background imports and loading separate from atlas frame loading, exactly as requested.
Add focused request-count evidence in Playwright rather than relying on a manually observed browser network panel.
Canonical gate combines the repository's lint, typecheck, unit test, build, desktop Playwright, and mobile smoke commands because no single existing script covers all requested checks.

packet.summary: Review deterministic two-theme atlas implementation. Baseline was clean except unrelated untracked opencode.json. This feature adds one executable atlas generator and eight generated artifacts (four WebP / four JSON), modifies runtime loading/rendering, unit coverage, package script, and task status. No deletions, renames, or executable-mode changes to tracked files; generated script is expected executable mode only if its creation preserves shebang defaults, which git inventory has not staged. `pnpm assets:atlas` was rerun with no generated diff, lint/typecheck/full unit suite passed, targeted sleeping companion E2E passed, and four atlases decode to 36,291,200 bytes versus 33,938,440 source bytes.

findings.summary: Companion atlases exceed the WebGL 2048 texture compatibility bound
findings.evidence: scripts/pack-runtime-atlases.mjs:18 and :73-121 pack four 512px rows plus five 2px gaps, producing 1544x2058 images; src/assets/runtime-atlases/light-companion.json:244-249 and dark-companion.json:244-249 confirm height 2058. A conforming 2048-max texture context cannot upload these atlases, so every companion frame can fail on affected mobile/older GPUs. The approved outcome explicitly requires bounded atlas dimensions and mobile behavior preservation.
